questionText: Which component of a computer system is primarily responsible for executing instructions and performing logical calculations?
text: Which component of a computer system is primarily responsible for executing instructions and performing logical calculations?
explanation: The CPU executes program instructions and does arithmetic/logic (inside it, the ALU). RAM only holds data temporarily, the HDD stores data permanently, and the motherboard only connects the parts.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of an IP address in a computer network?
text: What is the primary purpose of an IP address in a computer network?

options.text: To identify the physical location of the user
To uniquely identify a device connected to a network
To provide power to network interfaces

explanation: An IP address identifies a device (its network interface) so packets can be routed to it. It does not reveal the user’s physical location, does not encrypt anything and has nothing to do with power.

questionText: Which of the following best describes the function of Random Access Memory (RAM)?
text: Which of the following best describes the function of Random Access Memory (RAM)?

options.text: It permanently stores the operating system.
It acts as volatile, temporary storage for data actively being used.
It handles long-term archival of documents.
It connects the computer to a local network.

explanation: RAM is volatile (loses its content without power) temporary storage for the data and programs in use right now. Permanent storage of the OS and archives is the job of disks/flash; connecting to a network is the job of the network card.

questionText: Which service is responsible for translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses?
text: Which service is responsible for translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses?
explanation: DNS works like a phone book: it turns a name such as nptel.ac.in into an IP address. DHCP hands out IP addresses, FTP transfers files, HTTP transfers web pages.

questionText: A network that connects computers and devices within a limited physical area, such as a single office building or a university laboratory, is known as a:
text: A network that connects computers and devices within a limited physical area, such as a single office building or a university laboratory, is known as a:
explanation: A LAN covers one building, office or lab. PAN is only a few metres around a person, MAN covers a city, WAN covers countries.

questionText: In the context of a basic computing architecture, which of the following acts as an input device (analogous to a sensor in an IoT system)?
text: In the context of a basic computing architecture, which of the following acts as an input device (analogous to a sensor in an IoT system)?
explanation: A keyboard brings information into the computer, exactly as a sensor brings measurements into an IoT system. Printer, monitor and speaker are output devices (they correspond to actuators).

questionText: A Media Access Control (MAC) address is a hardware identification number typically hard-coded into which component?
text: A Media Access Control (MAC) address is a hardware identification number typically hard-coded into which component?
explanation: The MAC address is burned into the network adapter, the NIC (or the radio chip). The CPU, power supply and BIOS do not carry the network hardware address.

questionText: At the most fundamental hardware level, how is all digital data represented inside a computer?
text: At the most fundamental hardware level, how is all digital data represented inside a computer?
explanation: Electronic circuits store and process everything as bits, 0 and 1. Hexadecimal is only a human shorthand for writing bits; characters are coded in bits; continuous waves are analog, not digital.

questionText: Which networking device operates by examining incoming data packets and determining the best path to forward them to their destination across different networks?
text: Which networking device operates by examining incoming data packets and determining the best path to forward them to their destination across different networks?
explanation: A router reads the destination address of each packet and picks the best path between different networks. A hub blindly repeats, a switch forwards within one LAN, and an access point only gives wireless access.

questionText: What does the term "Cloud Storage" fundamentally refer to in basic internet architecture?
text: What does the term "Cloud Storage" fundamentally refer to in basic internet architecture?

options.text: Storing data on a localized external hard drive attached to a router
Storing data on remote servers managed by a provider and accessed via the internet
Compacting and zipping files to save space on a hard drive
Temporarily saving data in the computer’s RAM

explanation: Cloud storage means your data sits on remote servers run by a provider and is reached over the Internet. A local external drive, zipping files or RAM are all local.

questionText: What is the primary function of an Operating System (OS)?
text: What is the primary function of an Operating System (OS)?

options.text: To protect the computer from physical hardware theft
To manage computer hardware resources and provide common services for computer programs
To translate foreign languages on web pages
To physically cool the CPU during heavy workloads

explanation: The operating system manages hardware (CPU, memory, files, devices) and gives common services to programs. It does not prevent theft, translate languages or cool the CPU.

questionText: In a web browser’s URL bar, what does the "s" in HTTPS signify?
text: In a web browser’s URL bar, what does the "s" in HTTPS signify?
explanation: HTTPS = HTTP Secure: the connection is encrypted with TLS.

questionText: Before a real-world physical metric (like temperature) can be processed by a computer, an analog signal must usually pass through which component?
text: Before a real-world physical metric (like temperature) can be processed by a computer, an analog signal must usually pass through which component?
explanation: A sensor produces an analog signal; an ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) turns it into numbers the processor can use. A DAC goes the other way (digital to analog), the ALU calculates, and USB is only a connection.

questionText: What does the acronym URL stand for?
text: What does the acronym URL stand for?
explanation: URL = Uniform Resource Locator, the address of a resource on the web.

questionText: Which protocol is the foundational standard for transmitting web pages and data over the World Wide Web?
text: Which protocol is the foundational standard for transmitting web pages and data over the World Wide Web?
explanation: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of the World Wide Web. FTP is for files, SMTP for e-mail and SSH for secure remote login.

questionText: Which sensor can detect gases like LPG, CH4, and CO?
text: Which sensor can detect gases like LPG, CH4, and CO?
explanation: The slide lists “Gas (LPG, CH4 and CO) detector sensor – MQ-5”. DHT22 measures temperature and humidity, HC-SR04 is the ultrasonic distance sensor, and PIR detects motion (body heat). (Lecture 1, slide 6.)

questionText: Which modulation scheme does Zigbee use for the 2.4 GHz band?
text: Which modulation scheme does Zigbee use for the 2.4 GHz band?
explanation: ZigBee uses BPSK in the lower bands (868 and 902–928 MHz) and OQPSK (Offset Quadrature Phase Shift Keying) in the 2.4 GHz band, giving 250 kbps. (Lecture 2, slide 12.)

questionText: What does the Constrained RESTful Environments (CoRE) framework include for service discovery?
text: What does the Constrained RESTful Environments (CoRE) framework include for service discovery?

options.text: REST based protocols such as HTTP and CoAP

explanation: In CoRE service discovery, IoT devices register their resources with the Resource Directory (RD) through the Registration Interface (RI), and the RI supports REST-based protocols such as HTTP and CoAP. All three are part of the framework. (Lecture 4, slide 10.)

questionText: What is the maximum data rate of Z-Wave communication technology?
text: What is the maximum data rate of Z-Wave communication technology?
explanation: Z-Wave offers a data rate of up to 100 kbps with an average range of 30 m. 250 kbps is the 2.4 GHz rate of IEEE 802.15.4/ZigBee; 1 Mbps is Bluetooth 1.2. (Lecture 3, slide 4.)

questionText: Which protocol is CoAP based on?
text: Which protocol is CoAP based on?
explanation: CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) works on a request/response model over UDP, secured with DTLS. It is RESTful like HTTP but is not built on HTTP or TCP. (Lecture 5, slide 10.)

questionText: Which coding scheme is used by the IEEE 802.15.4 standard for transmitting information?
text: Which coding scheme is used by the IEEE 802.15.4 standard for transmitting information?
explanation: IEEE 802.15.4 uses the DSSS (Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum) coding scheme, which makes it tolerant to noise and interference. CSS is only an optional PHY added in amendment 802.15.4a; THSS (time-hopping spread spectrum) and OFDM are not used. (Lecture 2, slide 5.)

questionText: What does ’Range’ indicate in a sensor?
text: What does ’Range’ indicate in a sensor?

options.text: The smallest change in input that can be detected
The difference between the standard value and the value produced by the sensor
The highest and the lowest value of the physical quantity within which the sensor can actually sense

explanation: Range is the highest and lowest value of the quantity within which the sensor can sense. Option A describes accuracy, B describes resolution and C describes error. (Lecture 1, slide 8.)

questionText: Which organization has developed the ISA 100.11a standard?
text: Which organization has developed the ISA 100.11a standard?
explanation: ISA100.11a was developed by the International Society of Automation (ISA). (The ISA’s old name was “Instrument Society of America”, which is the trap in option A.) (Lecture 3, slide 8.)

questionText: Which of the following is/are the drawbacks of proprietary non-IP-based solutions?
text: Which of the following is/are the drawbacks of proprietary non-IP-based solutions?
explanation: The slide lists all three drawbacks of proprietary non-IP solutions: limited flexibility to end users (vendor-specific APIs), interoperability problems (vendor-specific sensors and gateways), and limited last-mile connectivity. (Lecture 4, slide 6.)

questionText: Which MQTT QoS Level is also known as “at most once” delivery?
text: Which MQTT QoS Level is also known as “at most once” delivery?
explanation: MQTT QoS 0 = at most once (best effort, no acknowledgement, no retry). QoS 1 = at least once; QoS 2 = exactly once. (Lecture 5, slide 7.)

questionText: Fill in the blank space designated by the question mark in the transducer block diagram (Input signal -> Sensor -> ? -> Actuator -> Output signal).
text: Fill in the blank space designated by the question mark in the transducer block diagram (Input signal -> Sensor -> ? -> Actuator -> Output signal).
explanation: In the transducer block diagram the chain is Input signal → Sensor → Processor → Actuator → Output signal. The processor interprets the sensor’s data and commands the actuator. Snubbers, repeaters and amplifiers are not part of this diagram. (Lecture 1, slide 2.)

questionText: Which of the following best describes a vector sensor?
text: Which of the following best describes a vector sensor?

options.text: Its response depends only on the temperature.
Its response depends only on the magnitude of the input.
Its response depends on the magnitude, direction, and orientation of the input parameter.
Its response is independent of the input parameter.

explanation: A vector sensor’s response depends on the magnitude, direction and orientation of the input (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetic field, motion). Option B describes a scalar sensor. (Lecture 1, slide 20.)

questionText: Which of the following frequency ranges is used by 6LoWPAN worldwide?
text: Which of the following frequency ranges is used by 6LoWPAN worldwide?
explanation: 6LoWPAN operates at 2400–2483.5 MHz worldwide and at 902–929 MHz in North America only. (Lecture 2, slide 17.)

questionText: In DDS RTPS, data is referred to as:
text: In DDS RTPS, data is referred to as:
explanation: In DDS RTPS, data is termed “topics”, and listeners subscribe to the topics they are interested in. (Lecture 5, slide 22.)

questionText: Which of the following IoT protocols is based on the session layer of the OSI model?
text: Which of the following IoT protocols is based on the session layer of the OSI model?
explanation: The official key is D (DTLS). The answer comes from the course textbook (Misra, Roy and Mukherjee, page 7), not from the slides. Why it fits: in the OSI model, TLS-type security protocols are usually placed at the session layer (layer 5), because they set up and manage a secure session between two ends; DTLS is the UDP version of TLS. MQTT, CoAP and AMQP are application-layer messaging protocols in the slides. Remember this pairing exactly: “session layer → DTLS”.

questionText: What is a transducer? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: What is a transducer? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)

options.text: A device that converts energy from one form to another
A type of sensor that detects only energy
A part of a computer processor

explanation: A transducer converts a signal/energy from one physical form to another.

questionText: What does sensor accuracy refer to? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: What does sensor accuracy refer to? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)

options.text: The correctness of the output compared to a standard value

explanation: Accuracy = correctness of output compared with a standard (superior) system.

questionText: What is an active sensor? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: What is an active sensor? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)

options.text: A sensor that can only sense physical changes
A sensor that operates without an external power source
A sensor that independently senses the input
A sensor that operates without any energy consumption

explanation: Active sensors sense independently (radar, sounder, laser altimeter).

questionText: What does ‘Actuator’ primarily refer to in IIoT systems? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: What does ‘Actuator’ primarily refer to in IIoT systems? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)

options.text: A device that converts signals into physical action
A device that enhances signal strength

explanation: An actuator turns a control signal plus energy into physical action (motion/force).

questionText: Zigbee technology is popular for ________. (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Zigbee technology is popular for ________. (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: ZigBee: low cost, low power, low data rate; mesh is its most popular topology.

questionText: Which of the following is true about 6LoWPAN? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Which of the following is true about 6LoWPAN? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)

options.text: It is used for high-power industrial networks
It enables IPv6 packets over low-power wireless networks
It’s a standard for satellite communications

explanation: 6LoWPAN = IPv6 over Low-Power WPANs.

questionText: Near Field Communication (NFC) is typically used for: (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Near Field Communication (NFC) is typically used for: (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)

options.text: Short-range wireless interaction between electronic devices

explanation: NFC works at less than 10 cm.

questionText: Which of the following actuators work on the principle of compression and decompression? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Which of the following actuators work on the principle of compression and decompression? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: Hydraulic (fluid power) actuators use pressurised fluid; compressing the fluid in a cylinder moves the piston.

questionText: What is the maximum data rate possible in Wireless HART? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: What is the maximum data rate possible in Wireless HART? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: WirelessHART: 2.4 GHz, up to 250 kb/s.

questionText: QoS 2 in MQTT is also known as ____________. (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: QoS 2 in MQTT is also known as ____________. (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: QoS 0 at most once, 1 at least once, 2 exactly once.

questionText: Infra-red sensor is an example of __________. (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Infra-red sensor is an example of __________. (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: Infrared is light, so an IR sensor is an optical sensor.

questionText: Which Zigbee device type acts as the root and also functions as the network bridge? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Which Zigbee device type acts as the root and also functions as the network bridge? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: The coordinator is the root; it starts the network and bridges it to others.

questionText: What is the data rate of Bluetooth 2.0? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: What is the data rate of Bluetooth 2.0? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: 1 Mbps (v1.2), 3 Mbps (v2.0).

text: A Bluetooth piconet can contain at most
explanation: One master + seven slaves.

questionText: What is a significant characteristic of new materials in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
text: What is a significant characteristic of new materials in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
explanation: On the “New Materials” slide, the new materials of the fourth revolution are lighter, stronger, recyclable and adaptive (examples: thermoset plastics, graphene). (Lecture 6, slide 19.)

questionText: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?
text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution?

options.text: Extensive use of the ubiquitous and mobile internet
Use of artificial intelligence and machine learning

explanation: The steam engine drove the first industrial revolution (1760–1840). The mobile Internet, AI/ML and CPS are all listed characteristics of the fourth. (Lecture 6, slide 5.)

questionText: What is considered the main nervous system of any manufacturing industry?
text: What is considered the main nervous system of any manufacturing industry?
explanation: The slide calls ICT (Information and Communication Technology) “the main nervous system of any manufacturing industry”: without it there is no communication within the enterprise. (Lecture 7, slide 7.)

questionText: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a sustainable industry?
text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a sustainable industry?
explanation: A sustainable industry provides energy efficiency, conservation of resources and low-waste production. Depending on government subsidies is not listed and is not sustainable. (Lecture 7, slide 2.)

questionText: What does L, D and T stand for under ‘People Engagement’ in the Lean production System?
text: What does L, D and T stand for under ‘People Engagement’ in the Lean production System?
explanation: People engagement in lean follows Learn (clear knowledge of tools), Do (perform all tools), Teach (become a teacher of the tools). (Lecture 8, slide 15.)

questionText: Which resource is associated with the ’Optimization’ categorization of Smart and connected products?
text: Which resource is associated with the ’Optimization’ categorization of Smart and connected products?
explanation: The “Optimization” category of smart and connected products uses optimization algorithms as its resource; its effects are better performance, remote services and help with repair. (Lecture 9, slide 9.)

questionText: State True or False. The amalgamation of CPS and the evolution of Internet-based technologies led to the development of the Industrial Internet.
text: State True or False. The amalgamation of CPS and the evolution of Internet-based technologies led to the development of the Industrial Internet.
explanation: True. The course textbook explains that combining cyber-physical systems with Internet-based technologies produced the Industrial Internet. This matches the course’s general story: CPS plus Internet connectivity gives IIoT.

questionText: State True or False. Real-time supply chain monitoring reduces inventory and capital requirements.
text: State True or False. Real-time supply chain monitoring reduces inventory and capital requirements.
explanation: True. Real-time supply chain monitoring lets a company see stock and shipments as they move, so it can keep less inventory and therefore tie up less capital. (Course textbook, p. 40. The same idea appears in the course’s lean “inventory waste” and just-in-time concepts.)

questionText: In the context of Industry 4.0, what is the full form of CPS?
text: In the context of Industry 4.0, what is the full form of CPS?
explanation: CPS = Cyber-Physical Systems: physical machines tightly integrated with computing and networking. (Lecture 6, slide 5.)

questionText: What does ERP stand for in the context of ICT?
text: What does ERP stand for in the context of ICT?
explanation: ERP = Enterprise Resource Planning, listed as an example of ICT. (Lecture 7, slide 7.)

questionText: What is a ’value stream’ in Lean Production System?.
text: What is a ’value stream’ in Lean Production System?.

options.text: A set of tools for production
All the actions required for a product from order to delivery

explanation: A value stream is all the actions required for a product from order to delivery. (Lecture 8, slide 7.)

questionText: Which of the following are key attributes of a smart business model?
text: Which of the following are key attributes of a smart business model?

options.text: Manual processes, cost reduction, and labor dependency
Value proposition, revenue streams, and technologies
Traditional marketing, fixed costs, and limited innovation
Centralized control, non-digital strategies, and fixed processes

explanation: The three key attributes of a smart business model are value proposition, revenue streams and technologies. (Lecture 9, slide 12.)

questionText: Which of the following is not a component of a Smart Factory?
text: Which of the following is not a component of a Smart Factory?
explanation: Smart factory components: smart machines, smart devices, smart manufacturing processes, smart engineering, information technology, data analysis, innovation. Physical (paper) ledgers are the opposite of smart. (Lecture 10, slide 5.)

questionText: In which format is healthcare data transmitted to maintain data uniformity and interoperability?
text: In which format is healthcare data transmitted to maintain data uniformity and interoperability?
explanation: HL7 (Health Level Seven) is the international standard format for exchanging healthcare data between hospital systems, giving uniformity and interoperability. “Level Seven” refers to layer 7 (application) of the OSI model. (Course textbook, p. 41.)

questionText: What are the key characteristics of agility?
text: What are the key characteristics of agility?
explanation: Agility in a smart factory = flexibility, adaptation and self-configuration. (Lecture 10, slide 16.)

questionText: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
text: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the Fourth Industrial Revolution? (earlier-year assignment, Jan–Apr 2024, Jan–Apr 2026)
explanation: Fourth revolution: AI, ML, CPS, mobile Internet, cheap sensors. Steam was the 1st; assembly line the 2nd.

questionText: What does "reactive computation" in CPS signify?
text: What does "reactive computation" in CPS signify?

options.text: Interaction with the environment in an ongoing manner

explanation: Reactive computation means the CPS interacts with its environment in an ongoing manner: a continuous sequence of observed inputs and outputs. It does not mean zero response time, fixed predefined computation or isolation. (Lecture 11, slide 6.)

questionText: Fill in the blanks. In healthcare applications, CPS is used for __________.
text: Fill in the blanks. In healthcare applications, CPS is used for __________.
explanation: CPS healthcare applications include highly accurate medical devices and image-guided surgery and therapy. Manual monitoring, static management systems and front-desk work are not CPS. (Lecture 11, slide 8.)

questionText: Which level in the "5C Architecture" ensures the gathering of precise status information of machines?
text: Which level in the "5C Architecture" ensures the gathering of precise status information of machines?
explanation: The Cyber level is the central information hub. It gathers information from the fleet of machines and obtains precise status information of individual machines, rates each machine and predicts future behaviour. Conversion turns data into information; Cognition presents knowledge; Configuration gives supervisory control. (Lecture 11, slide 15.)

questionText: Fill in the blanks. Intelligent sensors are capable of __________________.
text: Fill in the blanks. Intelligent sensors are capable of __________________.

options.text: Processing sensed data and managing external sensors/devices

explanation: Intelligent sensors can process sensed data, customise embedded algorithms on the fly and manage/control external sensors and devices. “Only sensing” or basic ADC describes ordinary sensors. (Lecture 11, slide 23.)

questionText: How many steps are there in the PLM solution approach in Industry 4.0?
text: How many steps are there in the PLM solution approach in Industry 4.0?
explanation: “The Ten Step Approach: PLM solution in Industry 4.0” has ten steps, from data gathering to executive decision support. (Lecture 12, slide 24.)

questionText: Which of the following is not a key component of an AR Device?
text: Which of the following is not a key component of an AR Device?
explanation: Key components of AR devices: sensors and cameras, projection screen, processing unit, reflection (mirrors). A remote control is not listed. (Lecture 13, slide 8.)

questionText: Which of the following is NOT a challenge of AI in IIoT?
text: Which of the following is NOT a challenge of AI in IIoT?
explanation: The four challenges of AI in IIoT are connecting devices, understanding data, training AI and making it actionable. Lack of data is not a challenge, because IIoT generates huge amounts of data. (Lecture 14, slide 13.)

questionText: Which of the following is not one of the primary constraints of mobile CPS?
text: Which of the following is not one of the primary constraints of mobile CPS?
explanation: The textbook (Section 2.3.2) lists the constraints of mobile CPS as network stability, power requirement and security. Design aesthetics is not an engineering constraint.

questionText: What are the components of the 5C architecture for CPS?
text: What are the components of the 5C architecture for CPS?
explanation: The 5C architecture = Connection, Conversion, Cyber, Cognition, Configuration. (Also on Lecture 11, slide 13.)

questionText: What is one of the key features of CPS in terms of computation?
text: What is one of the key features of CPS in terms of computation?
explanation: Reactive computation is the first listed feature of CPS (with concurrency, feedback control, real-time computation and safety-critical applications). (Lecture 11, slide 6.)

questionText: What is a collaboration platform in the context of Industry 4.0?
text: What is a collaboration platform in the context of Industry 4.0?

options.text: A type of business software that combines organizational networking capacities with operations

questionText: Active RFID tags are classified into which two types?

explanation: Active RFID tags are of two types: transponders (wake up and respond when they receive a reader’s signal) and beacons (broadcast their signal periodically). The slides only say active tags “broadcast information in the form of beacons”, so the classification is standard RFID knowledge, not slide text. It is confirmed by a 2024 assignment of this course, whose answer was “Transponders and beacons are types of active RFID tags” (see P11-14).
